record.file_problem: The input contains repository metadata, README, and file list only. It is not garbled; referenced files such as results/report.md are not included.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports outcomes from OBLITERATUS abliteration runs, including refusal and capability-related metrics. This bears on practical removal (V2), but it does not report the original difference-in-means intervention or a replication of it.
record.gate_note: The README reports two OBLITERATUS runs and describes abliteration generally as orthogonal projection on weights or activations. It does not specify the run-level projection details, a baseline refusal rate, or whether the table's refusal metric used markers or a judge. The referenced detailed report is not present.
record.test_reason: The README reports two real OBLITERATUS abliteration runs on released models (Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3, Qwen3-8B), with post-edit refusal and capability proxies. That bears weakly on V2. There are no pre-edit baselines, refusal is scored by markers, and the run-level edit details are not given.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The README presents ALBLATOR as a unified tool for running and benchmarking abliteration methods. It argues that refusal rate alone misleads and must be screened against perplexity, coherence and capability. Its example shows the Mistral run passing and the Qwen3-8B run rejected as over-ablated. The authoritative GPU evaluation and full campaign are future work.
record.recipe_differences: This is a tooling repository that runs and compares Heretic, OBLITERATUS, and ErisForge; the README does not specify use of the original difference-in-means direction or the original intervention recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported screening outcome differs by model and preset: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 with advanced passes; Qwen3-8B with informed fails as over-ablated.
record.problems: Only two example runs are reported. No unabliterated baselines, uncertainty estimates, or detailed run-level edit are given. The README says refusal is currently scored by markers and capabilities by perplexity, while the authoritative GPU evaluation is still pending.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows reported in the provided README. The referenced results/report.md and result files are listed but their contents are not included.

untested.parts: Pre-edit refusal baselines; judge-based refusal (Llama-Guard-3) and lm-eval capability evaluations are stated as future work; Heretic and ErisForge runs on real models; the Ministral-8B runs.
No difference-in-means direction, ablation or addition test.
Qwen3-8B can reason before answering, but no thinking-mode analysis is reported.

missing.what: First-token KL base vs abliterated: 2.25 for Mistral advanced, Inf for Qwen3-8B informed
Detailed run results and the samples' JSON (not included in text)

record.verdict_notes: This is a tooling repo with two illustrative runs, so the evidence is very thin. No Mistral verdict is given: the 0.13 post-edit refusal rate has no baseline and comes from marker scoring. The instruct model may have refused little to begin with. Capability rows are linked to V2 only as costs of the edit.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means direction is measured, ablated at every layer and position, or added; no test of refusal induction or preservation of other abilities by that intervention.
No refusal baseline is reported, and the table does not state the exact weight edit or whether each output model was released. The README does not establish refusal removal against a pre-edit model.
No jailbreak mechanism or adversarial training against ablation is evaluated.
No comparison of single-direction, affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No cross-language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or timing.
